newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end mixed, nearbys up on Brazil talk.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end mixed, nearbys up on Brazil talk.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended mixed with nearby months propped up by rumors Brazil was planning to impose an export tax on soybeans and soymeal, traders said.

"There was talk Brazil might reinstitute some kind of export tax," Bob Lekberg, analyst with Goldenberg-Hehmeyer, said. "This is the same talk that floated around a few weeks ago. In the final wash, I think it won't go through."

Neither Brazil's agricultural nor finance ministries knew of a proposal. "The Finance Ministry is not formulating any proposal to put a tax on soybean or soymeal exports and knows of no proposal to do so," a spokesman there said.

Old crop contracts were further bolstered by talk several analytical firms cut soybean production estimates for Brazil and Argentina. They said estimates for Brazil's output ranged from 25.8 million to 26.3 million tonnes, all below USDA's April prediction for 27.0 million.
They said estimates for Argentina output ranged from 11.0 million to 12.5 million tonnes, again below USDA's outlook for 13.25 million tonnes.
Soybeans ended 2-3/4 cents per bushel higher to 4-3/4 cents lower with July up 2-1/2 at $8.92 a bushel and new crop November down 2-1/4 at $7.01-1/4.

News early Tuesday that a clearing firm had incorrectly posted 1.160 million bushels of soybeans for delivery lent support to the May contract. CBOT said Iowa Grain must make delivery even though the bushels were posted in error.
Floor sources said Iowa Grain contacted the stoppers and made arrangements with several to buy the bushels back at a premium, thereby satisfying CBOT requirements.
New crop contracts were pressured by active U.S. soybean seeding progress as evidenced in Monday's USDA weekly crop progress.
USDA said soybean plantings were nine percent completed as of Sunday, above trade expectations for three to five percent.

Commodity funds were aggressive sellers of corn and wheat on the day but were noticeably absent from the sell-side in soybeans, pit sources said. On the day, Prudential Securities bought two million bushels July, Dean Witter bought one million July and one million November and Iowa Grain bought 1.5 million November.

In options trade, Louis Dreyfus bought 600 August $8.25 puts at 28-1/2 to 29 cents. Continental Grain bought 400 July $9.75 calls and sold 400 July $8.75 calls at 27 to 29-1/2 cents, pit sources said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 60,000 contracts, compared with Monday's actual volume of 67,891.
